evidence.t: Deer here are black tailed deer, the coast form of mule deer: the synopsis calls them "mule (black-tailed) deer" (99%, Rule Book: Region 2 Lower Mainland).
Mule deer winter range u-2-006 unit CQ 1-3 (official), 230 m SE. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2007 (19 years old), right here.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHms4): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
SW facing slope, 16 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Private fields 1.2 km S: deer feed on field edges (fields are private).
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

plan: Drive: from City of Delta, about 177 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 49.5081, -121.23508, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 190 m SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 0 m, about 5 min at 3 km/h.
Hunt: deer, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Watch the edge of the 2007 cutblock (right here) at first and last light. Sit above it with the wind in your face and glass (Tip).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 165 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 2-17, Region 2. Season: mule deer bucks Sept 10 to Dec 15 and more rows (synopsis page 28, 99%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R2A-deer-drive-0005.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 2-17: about 511 hunter days a year for mule deer and white tailed deer (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.50 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.2 km and about 0 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
